messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: cross-region routing anomaly detected

incident-bot: severity=P1 · elevated 5xx for EU traffic being routed to APAC hosts; DNS NXDOMAIN spikes observed from EU PoPs
incident-bot: affected endpoints: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings
incident-bot: first seen: 2026-03-15T13:52:00Z

sarah: ack — I'm on initial triage. paging @jia @emily @mike. Are we seeing many customers?

jia: checking control-plane. quick summary: two policy promotions for "latency-surge-policy" at 2026-03-15T13:45Z and 2026-03-15T13:50Z. The 13:50Z promotion injected an override mapping that directs eu-* prefixes to ap-east1 with ttl=45 while previous version had eu routing ttl=600.

emily: runtime telemetry: increased TLS handshakes failures and connection resets from certain EU POPs aligning with time of second promotion. p99 latency jumped to ~2.4s; error spike started at 13:51Z.

mike: metrics snapshot: global 5xx up from 0.6% baseline to 9.8% at 13:52Z. Top impacted regions show EU client IPs with traces landing in APAC hosts.

jia: debugging commands I'm running:

```bash
# fetch policy versions
curl -s 'https://controlplane.internal/api/policies/latency-surge-policy/versions' | jq -r '.[] | "{version: \(.version), when: \(.created_at), by: \(.created_by)}"'
# show active mappings
curl -s 'https://controlplane.internal/api/routes?policy=latency-surge-policy' | jq '.routes[] | {prefix,region,ttl,priority}'
```

jia: sample routes (sanitized):
- {prefix: "eu-north1/*", region: "ap-east1", ttl: 45, priority: 50}
- {prefix: "eu-north1/*", region: "eu-north1", ttl: 600, priority: 100}

emily: that priority inversion will cause some edge controllers to prefer the lower-ttl/ap-east1 mapping until their cache expirs; the mix explains oscillating NXDOMAINs and intermittent TLS mismatches.

sarah: mitigation plan: immediate rollback to prior stable policy version; set an emergency pin for eu-* to eu-north1 with ttl=600 to speed consistency; @jia execute rollback, @mike monitor, @emily coordinate graceful retries at runtime to avoid client errors.

jia: running rollback now:

```bash
rbctl promote --policy latency-surge-policy --from-version stable-20260315-01 --note "rollback due to priority inversion"
```

deploy-bot: Rollback job queued (id=cb7a1). Propagating to edge controllers. estimated global propagation ~75s.

mike: visible improvement already: 5xx at 13:54Z down from 9.8% to 3.7%. p95 latency falling toward baseline.

cust-success-bot: top impacted orgs (last 10m):
- org-6621 (high) — 13% error rate
- org-7102 (med) — 7.2% error rate
- org-1938 (low) — 6.1% error rate

cust-success-bot: recommended outreach: notify affected accounts with a short incident summary and ETA to resolution (target <30m)

emily: runtime caches flushing as new mapping takes effect; still seeing a few stale PoPs with old mapping until their 45s TTL expire. recommending we keep monitoring for 10m and avoid further policy promotions in that window.

jia: propagation complete at ~2026-03-15T13:55:40Z per control-plane logs. Verified route table: eu prefixes now uniformly point to eu-north1 with ttl=600 and priority=100.

mike: final metrics at 13:58Z: 5xx at 0.5%, p99 latency back to baseline. No new errors in last 3m.

sarah: marking incident mitigated. Next steps:
- create postmortem ticket INC-1719672000-PM (assign: jia, emily)
- root cause: race during promotion that allowed lower-priority override with shorter ttl to slip through
- short-term: block overlapping prefix promotions during active windows; require validation that promotions don't introduce lower-priority conflicting entries
- long-term: implement atomic two-phase apply for route promotions and an automated canary to validate edge mapping consistency

emily: I'll open the postmortem and include a suggested test to simulate TTL priority inversions.

sarah: handing off watch to @alex for 1-hour follow-up. alex, pls join PM sync tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

alex: ack — i'll take the watch and join the postmortem.

sarah: closing pager. thanks for quick responses everyone :clap:

-- end of thread
